current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, subprocess-fallback execution adjudication, the family-check path CheckResult policy projection, bounded run_id plus per-test lineage digests, per-test canonical execution/observation JSON construction for ordinary bounded string/null fields, ArtifactStore payload/file digests through 65,536 bytes, compiler/source/manifest provenance file digests through the ArtifactStore bounded file adapter, using one MNCS request up to 14,336 bytes and retained MNCS streaming through 512 KiB after warm-up, and public result JSON formatting for bounded JSON value trees are MNCS-owned. The run-identity app constructs canonical JSON for bounded inputs; Python projects typed identity fields and retains compact-JSON compatibility for out-of-contract inputs. The result-identity batch app handles up to 16 payloads, 64 chunks, 65,536 bytes, and the 8,000,000-step limit. The stream app carries native SHA-256 state across ArtifactStore calls of at most 14,336 bytes each and at most five calls per artifact. After three bounded native application hashes in one ArtifactStore, a retained mncs-embed session calls the same pure MNCS identity and SHA-256 functions for payloads and artifact files through 512 KiB; provenance hashing uses the existing ArtifactStore stream for files above 14,336 bytes; each retained window contains at most 14,336 bytes and one MNCS function call. The final window finalizes in that same call; the retained Python adapter no longer calls SHA-256 initialization or finalization directly. Larger artifacts and inputs before warm-up use host hashlib; failed embedding also falls back to the established host or native-app path. Python reads files, enumerates and sorts directories, sends bounded chunks, writes artifacts, and supervises processes; for tree identities, ArtifactStore hashes leaves through mncs.test.result_identity_v1 when the directory has at most 128 entries, the request is within 65,536 bytes, and aggregate leaf bytes are at most 1 MiB. Files through 65,536 bytes use a native application or retained session; larger files through 512 KiB use a retained session after warm-up. Oversized or unavailable native leaf hashing reports an exact host fallback. mncs.test.library_tree_identity_v1 folds ordered path and leaf-digest records; filesystem traversal and leaf reads remain host responsibilities; source/provenance files above 65,536 bytes before warm-up, above 512 KiB, or after embedding failure retain host hashing; the Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries. Python no longer recursively projects runtime values into a typed-value node/edge tree. For built-in values with string keys admitted by a conservative 4,096-byte preflight, the Test key-order application receives unsorted compact JSON and returns compact JSON with keys ordered by decoded UTF-8 bytes. Python retains sorted compact encoding for larger documents, non-string mapping keys, unsupported container subclasses, and native bounds or budget fallback; the existing token formatter then owns pretty public-result emission. The Test-owned mncs.test.public_result_json_token_v1 consumes the compact document as UTF-8-safe bounded chunks, uses mncs.std.json_cursor.v1 to scan and traverse JSON tokens, verifies the source SHA-256 on each continuation, emits the indented public document in 8,192-byte output windows, and carries native cursor and output digest state. Compact input and output are each limited to 65,536 bytes; native bounds remain 512 values, depth 63, 64 object members, 256-byte keys, and 1,024-byte scalar text. Python verifies the packed-source digest before dispatch, rejoins output pages, writes the document, and independently checks its digest. Values outside native bounds or budget exhaustion retain the exact host compatibility formatter. The 33 KB public-result fixture and ordinary compile-failure and family-check consumers use the token applications and match independent JSON and SHA-256 expectations. Existing Stdlib cursor and SHA-256 functionality were sufficient; this migration required no duplicate Stdlib parser. The family-check response path now reuses serialized TestResult and CheckResult documents as raw JSON fragments, then MNCS tokenizes, validates, orders, pretty-prints, and hashes the composed envelope; Python no longer rebuilds and re-encodes those nested trees for the response. Python still decodes them for policy validation and CheckResult projection. The family CheckResult consumer now passes its retained TestResult JSON document to the Test-owned test-check-result-json-native application. MNCS parses and extracts the native-supported policy fields before invoking the existing CheckResult policy; Python does not build the typed projection request on that path. The CLI --check-result path also supplies its serialized result document. Python still decodes the result for its existing validation and opaque selection field, and retains the previous projection as fallback when the native cursor or 1,024-byte decoded-text-field bound does not admit a value. The existing Test JSON cursor and policy were sufficient, so no new Stdlib parser was added. The native extractor now decodes up to 1,024 UTF-8 bytes per text field; escaped raw spans up to 6,144 bytes are scanned in six bounded 1,024-byte blocks, carrying JSON escape and surrogate-pair state. Test identities above 256 bytes and an exact-1,024-byte escaped UTF-8 failure message are accepted by the native path. Longer failure messages still use the compatibility projection.
desired_direction: Extend the bounded native serializer and streaming identity capabilities through real consumers, while moving common text, collection, and typed-value projection mechanisms into reusable MNCS stdlib interfaces where migration requirements support them. Keep application policy and platform filesystem/process access at their existing ownership boundaries.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py::ResultIdentityEmbedHasher.digest_chunks sends bounded requests to Test-owned MNCS stream transitions; the final update returns the finalized SHA-256 digest in the same call. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_hashes_large_payloads_in_a_retained_mncs_session checks empty and exact-14,336-byte streams plus independent digests for a 512 KiB payload and a 393,233-byte file, confirms one transition per window with no direct SHA-256 init/finalize calls, confirms only three warm-up hashes launch the app, and verifies session cleanup. test_artifact_store_hashes_native_stream_limit_in_five_updates checks exact 65,536-byte payload and file inputs against independent digests using five updates each. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_keeps_large_files_on_host_after_session_warmup confirms the 512 KiB ceiling remains in force after the native session threshold is met. The provenance differential test warms the retained session, hashes bounded compiler, source, and manifest files through ArtifactStore, compares every digest with independent hashlib, and verifies the runner source uses the retained MNCS stream and the Unicode directory fixture compares the MNCS tree fold with an independent Python SHA-256 golden, while the real Test native and mncs-stdlib library roots verify 91 bounded leaf files through the retained MNCS session with no host leaf digest calls. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_compile_failure_runner_keeps_medium_public_result_native runs the ordinary compile-failure runner, records native application outcomes, rejects any compatibility serializer call for TestResult/CheckResult, and compares the emitted document to an independent JSON golden. The focused family-check dispatch test verifies native calls for both the CheckResult digest and success response and compares the response bytes with an independent Python JSON golden. The live compiler-backed family-check test selects the two declared behavioral identities, passes end to end through the native runner, compares the response bytes with the same independent golden, and verifies the CheckResult digest against its exact public JSON bytes. The expanded native-window regression serializes a 37,377-byte, 80-node deep result through 16 MNCS windows and matches the independent JSON golden; a 66,663-byte result above the 65,536-byte cap confirms zero native calls and compatibility output. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_structured_input_node_bound_keeps_compatibility_json confirms that a 33 KB output whose byte-array request crosses the 32,768-node transport limit is classified as an input bound and preserves exact compatibility bytes. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_native_key_order_matches_unicode_and_escaped_key_golden compares native ordering and public formatting with independent Python goldens; tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_packed_text_keeps_large_public_result_on_native_windows confirms the conservative preflight skips unsorted serialization for results outside the native key-order bound. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_family_check_response_sends_nested_results_as_raw_native_tokens compares the composed native output with an independent JSON/SHA-256 golden and verifies that both nested documents cross the boundary as raw JSON fragments; tests/test_runner.py::RunnerTests::test_family_check_digest_uses_native_public_result_serializer confirms the response avoids a second generic host serialization. The typed-value projection follow-up is covered by tests/test_check_result_projection.py: the normal family result asserts supported=true from the JSON-native application and compares the finished CheckResult with an independent expected object; escaped Unicode verifies native string decoding; a long UTF-8 failure message asserts the native bound triggers the existing compatible host fallback. tests/test_runner.py::RunnerTests::test_family_check_digest_uses_native_public_result_serializer verifies that the family consumer passes the packed retained TestResult document to the new app. The live compiler-backed family_check selection passed end to end. The current text-decoding bound is exercised by the same focused tests: a 322-byte test identity and an escaped UTF-8 failure message of exactly 1,024 decoded bytes both assert native support; a longer message asserts compatibility fallback. observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
title: Native token streaming removes Test typed-tree projection
why_insufficient: The bounded public serializer accepts at most 512 values, depth 63, 64 children per object, 256-byte keys, 1,024-byte scalar text, and 65,536 output bytes. Structured application inputs still cap at 32,768 nodes for genuinely large typed trees, but packed UTF-8 byte fields avoid one transport node per text byte; the 33 KB differential case now stays on the native window path. Larger or unsupported values retain the compatibility path. Python still compact-encodes runtime values and retains compatibility sorting outside native eligibility. The key-order application natively parses and orders supported string-key objects through a 4,096-byte input bound; the public token applications validate and format sorted documents, while Python reassembles output pages and writes public documents. The subprocess native-stream path remains capped at 65,536 bytes: the exact-65,536-byte payload/file differential test uses five native app updates per artifact. After three bounded native app hashes, the retained session handles artifacts through 512 KiB in windows of at most 14,336 bytes. Differential tests cover a 512 KiB payload and a 393,233-byte compiler artifact against independent hashlib digests. An uncapped self-suite run reached the real 13 MB compiler artifacts and was interrupted after 4:21 while the runner used about 150 MB RSS and remained CPU-bound; this run did not pass and provides no performance claim. The retained path is now capped at 512 KiB, with host streaming hashlib for larger artifacts, before warm-up, or when embedding is unavailable. The complete cross-repository evidence protocol and out-of-contract run-identity projection remain outside the native application surface. Python retains runtime-to-compact-JSON encoding and filesystem access and traversal; library leaves use explicit host fallback above 512 KiB per file, above 1 MiB aggregate leaf bytes, outside the 128-entry or 65,536-byte request bounds, before retained-session warm-up for files above 65,536 bytes, or after native failure. Source/provenance files retain host fallback above 65,536 bytes before warm-up, above 512 KiB, or when retained embedding is unavailable; inputs through 65,536 bytes retain the native-app fallback, and compatibility behavior for unsupported or over-bound inputs. The Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries. A normal compile-pass integration check exceeded Control's MCP request deadline at 2:07 while the first implementation routed library trees through repeated native hashes; it was stopped, did not pass, and provides no performance claim. The final ordered library-tree identity fold uses MNCS for up to 128 entries within the 65,536-byte request bound. Eligible leaf hashing now uses the existing MNCS result-identity path; filesystem traversal and reads remain host responsibilities, and every native bound or execution fallback is reported. After library hashing was restored to host, a second local compile-pass check remained CPU-bound at 3:35 and was terminated without a result. The slow phase is unknown; neither integration attempt passed. A new ordinary-runner reproduction isolated one budget failure to the JSON string and integer emitters scanning all 64 slots of json_emit.Writer.buf when only len bytes were live. Those loops now use the live byte range; the 8,042-byte result completes in the native window application within 8,000,000 steps and byte-matches an independent Python JSON golden. Broader input bounds and compatibility handling for unsupported values or actual native failures remain. CheckResult trees outside existing native bounds retain the compatibility JSON and digest path. Earlier live attempts that selected the full compiler self-suite exceeded the fixed 120-second inner-runner deadline and provide no full-suite or performance claim. The bounded live family-check selection of two declared behavioral tests passed end to end and its response bytes match the independent host JSON golden. Over-bound success envelopes and native-budget exhaustion retain the host formatter; infrastructure-failure envelopes remain host-formatted so diagnostics survive serializer setup failures. The family-check success envelope falls back to the host formatter outside existing serializer bounds or on native budget exhaustion. Infrastructure-failure envelopes remain host-formatted to preserve diagnostic output when native setup or execution fails. The public-result typed-tree projection has since been removed: packed JSON source is scanned by the existing Stdlib JSON cursor, the native continuation recomputes its source digest, and the Test consumer verifies emitted bytes against an independent formatter and digest. Remaining host responsibilities include compact JSON encoding, output page reassembly, file writes, and exact compatibility fallback outside native bounds. The family-check success path now avoids a second host traversal of its nested result trees by passing the existing JSON documents as raw fragments to MNCS. Python still decodes them once for validation and CheckResult projection; the generic public-result entrypoint still starts from Python values and must preserve non-string-key sort semantics before the JSON transport loses original key types.
workaround: The MNCS test-check-result-projection application owns CheckResult policy and reference construction; test-lineage-identity constructs and hashes ordinary per-test execution/observation JSON; test-run-identity constructs and hashes bounded canonical run identities; test-result-identity hashes bounded payload batches; test-result-identity-stream carries native SHA-256 state through bounded 14,336-byte windows for payloads and files up to 65,536 bytes in at most five calls; after three app-based artifact hashes, ArtifactStore reuses an embedded session through 512 KiB and validates, updates, and finalizes SHA state in one MNCS call per retained window, while preserving host streaming fallback above that bound, before warm-up, or when embedding is unavailable; test-public-result-json serializes values with conservative bounds up to 8,192 bytes, and test-public-result-json-window serializes larger bounded values while carrying SHA-256 state across pages through mncs.std.sha256.v1. The adapter respects native row, field, payload, page, byte, step, and stream-call limits, retains compatibility behavior outside them, and independently checks the final public-document digest; the host compatibility serializer preserves exact output if a bounded native public-result call reports budget_exhausted. manifest_provenance hashes files through 14,336 bytes with one bounded MNCS request and routes files through 512 KiB via ArtifactStore; after session warm-up, runner source uses the retained MNCS stream, while files above 65,536 bytes use host fallback before warm-up or if embedding is unavailable, and files above 512 KiB always use host; inputs through 65,536 bytes retain the native-app fallback. For bounded directories, ArtifactStore hashes eligible leaf bytes through `mncs.test.result_identity_v1` under the 1 MiB aggregate and 512 KiB per-file limits, then `mncs.test.library_tree_identity_v1` folds ordered relative names and leaf digests. The result reports leaf and tree implementations separately; out-of-bound, pre-warm, and native-failure cases retain the exact host fallback. Python keeps filesystem traversal and file reads. Python compact-encodes public values, reassembles unresolved-message and JSON pages, performs filesystem access and traversal, and falls back to host hashing for oversized or unavailable native inputs before serializing unsupported or over-bound public values. It also retains process supervision, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport. When the native process-outcome classifier cannot launch after the host observed a process-start failure or timeout, the adapter preserves that direct platform outcome as infrastructure_failure or timeout. The representative ordinary compile-failure result now completes through the MNCS window serializer at 8,000,000 steps and matches the Python JSON golden; compatibility serialization remains available for unsupported or out-of-bound values and native execution failures. Family-check CheckResult digest calculation uses the public-result serializer bytes when native bounds permit; host JSON and hashing remain for bound or budget fallback. Successful family-check response envelopes use the same bounded MNCS serializer and fall back to the host formatter for out-of-bounds trees or native budget exhaustion; infrastructure-failure envelopes remain host-formatted. Public-result token apps receive one compact JSON document as UTF-8-safe chunks, verify the source digest in MNCS, scan tokens with mncs.std.json_cursor.v1, and emit bounded JSON windows with native SHA-256 continuation. Python typed-tree projection is retired. For eligible string-key documents through 4,096 bytes, MNCS parses a bounded native value, orders its object keys, and returns compact JSON to the existing native public formatter. Python retains compact encoding, output-page reassembly, file writes, and exact sorted compatibility output for non-string keys, unsupported values, native limits, or budget exhaustion. The successful family-check response now reuses raw serialized TestResult and CheckResult fragments and sends the compact envelope through the MNCS token pipeline, removing the second Python traversal and encoding of those nested result trees. Python retains one decode for policy validation and CheckResult projection; compatibility output remains available when native bounds or budget do not admit the composed source. The new test-check-result-json-native application parses bounded retained TestResult JSON through the existing Test cursor, extracts supported fields into the unchanged native CheckResult policy request, and returns the policy projection directly. The family-check path and ordinary --check-result path pass their existing serialized document, avoiding Python typed field projection for admitted documents. The native extractor is bounded to 65,536 input bytes, 512 values, depth 12, 64 object members, 1,024 decoded bytes per text field, a 6,144-byte raw-span ceiling scanned in six bounded 1,024-byte blocks, and 256 test rows. Oversized strings, including longer failure messages, and unsupported shapes preserve the established host projection fallback; Python still retains the opaque selection object and one result decode for policy validation.
